newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign light crudes pricey, remain scarce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign light crudes pricey, remain scarce.

text.p: U.S. light crude imports remained scarce amid buoyant refiner demand for distillates and a still narrow arbitrage, traders said Thursday.
A VLCC fixed on subjects failed today, removing the possibility of upcoming Brent sales by a major to the U.S.
The last nominal price heard for delivered Brent was Dec West Texas Intermediate plus 90 cents cif Wednesday, but traders said that the level would not be feasible now.
Other North Sea and West African spot cargoes were not offered into the market, although several fixtures to the U.S. and South America were seen from West Africa.
Heavily discounted Canadian crudes continued to move into the U.S. Midwest, dislodging West Texas Sour at Midland.
"People are not fully appreciating how much the heavy Canadian API 22 crudes are squeezing the domestics," a Midwest refinery trader said.
Other heavy crudes included a Canadon Seco offered into the U.S. West Coast for December delivery. A firm price was not heard but a recent cargo traded at WTI minus $2.39 fob.
In late U.S. trade, details of more European fob sales surfaced confirming a softening trend, except for Dated Brent.
Three Forties traded for early/mid November between Dated Brent plus 30 to 25 cents fob.
Two refiners swapped dates for Oseberg, Nov 12-15 and 19-21 at Dated Brent plus 35 cents.
In the paper market, a full cargo of Jan Brent traded at $23.30 a barrel, up from the London IPE close at $23.12.
A Wall Street trader, meanwhile, bought several Jan Brent partials at $23.25 a barrel.
